headline: Rangers, James Reimer Contract Termination Echoes Historically Harsh Reality For Multiple Longtime NHL Goaltenders
take:
The Hockey News reports that the Rangers and goalie James Reimer have mutually agreed to terminate his contract, which the outlet says likely ends his NHL career. As Mollie Walker of the New York Post posted on Nov. 5, he had been placed on waivers, a step she tied to Joonas Korpisalo's impending return.

The numbers explain why the Rangers could move on. Reimer played one game for NYR this season and stopped .625 of the shots he faced. In goals saved above expected, which measures how many goals a goalie prevents compared with what an average goalie would allow on the same shots, he sits at -1.96 so far this season, worse than the -1.67 he posted over 14 games last year. That is a small sample, but it points the wrong way. The team itself is in decent shape: NYR is 9-7-1 and controls 52.5 percent of expected goals, our measure of chance quality. Its goals-minus-expected figure is -5.4, so shooting has lagged the chances, while the goaltending as a group is +2 in goals saved above expected. Losing Reimer changes little on the ice.
